learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge and use of the principles of circuit theory and electrical machines.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of electronics.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of automation and control methods.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Structure the discourse to favor the understanding of the objectives, actions and/or results of one's own work.
Develop professional texts or scientific-technical reports according to the conventions of the discipline.
Solve complex problems, autonomously, in the field of the discipline.

teaching_methods: Expository class (participatory lecture, conferences, company visits, trade fair attendance)
Laboratory (activities in specialized spaces, research sessions on classroom didactics)
Integrated project (problem-solving, task-addressing through planning, design, and execution)
Tutoring (personalized and small group attention, review, reorientation of class materials, learning, and work completion)
Group work (individual and group preparation of essays, problem-solving, projects for submission and presentation)
Individual work (student study: preparation of readings, exams, exercises, class preparation)
assessment_rules: The final grade (N_F) is calculated as: 0.25·N_PI + 0.15·N_TA + 0.3·N_P1 + 0.3·N_P2. To pass the course in any ordinary call, a grade of 5 or higher (N_F ≥ 5) is required, along with a grade of 4 or higher in both partial exams (N_P1 and N_P2) or in the final exam (N_EX). If these conditions are not met, the course will be failed, with a maximum final grade of 4. In the second call (resit), the N_PI grade is maintained, N_TA can be recovered via a theory/practical test, and N_P1 and N_P2 can be recovered through a single written exam (N_EX), requiring a minimum score of 4. The resit formula is N_F = 0.25·N_PI + 0.15·N_TA + 0.6·N_EX.
